is_anopheles.evidence: The paper studies the codling moth, Cydia pomonella (Lepidoptera: Tortricidae), which is an agricultural pest, not an Anopheles malaria vector.

reports_target_markers.evidence: The paper reports on the L1014F mutation in the codling moth (Cydia pomonella), not in Anopheles mosquitoes.

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: The paper provides genotype counts and allele frequencies for codling moth populations in Tables 1 and 2.

african_field_population.evidence: The study focuses on codling moth populations, not Anopheles mosquitoes.

is_primary_study.evidence: This is a primary empirical study.

sub_country_location.evidence: The paper provides data at the orchard level for South-eastern France (Table 2).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Collection years are provided for each sample (Table 1).

duplicate_risk.evidence: The study reports new collections and analyses.

supplement.evidence: All necessary data is provided in the main text and tables.

assessment.summary: This paper investigates the L1014F kdr mutation in the codling moth (Cydia pomonella) across 19 countries. It is not eligible because it does not study Anopheles malaria vectors.
